issue.title: read_line_range tool reports line count off-by-one vs wc -l
issue.body:
## Bug

The read_line_range tool (and read_file with line ranges) reports total line counts that are off-by-one compared to wc -l.

## Reproduction

For a file where wc -l reports 2,237 lines:

    wc -l packages/core/src/config/config.ts
    2237 packages/core/src/config/config.ts

The read_line_range tool reports:

    Status: Showing lines 1-200 of 2238 total lines.

Similarly for a 1,386-line file (wc -l), the tool reports 1387.

## Impact

This caused a code review agent (deepthinker) to repeatedly flag accurate line counts in plan documents as wrong because it trusted the tool output over the documented counts. Multiple review iterations were wasted chasing phantom off-by-one errors.

## Likely Cause

The tool probably counts a trailing newline as an extra line, or uses a 1-based-inclusive range calculation that adds 1 to the total. wc -l counts newline characters, so a file ending with a newline has N newlines = N lines. The tool may be counting N+1 by treating the position after the last newline as an additional line.

## Expected Behavior

read_line_range total line count should match wc -l for the same file.

steps: Use read_line_range to read lines 1-200 of f.txt and report the total line count it shows.
expected: read_line_range reports the same total as wc -l, i.e. `Showing lines 1-200 of 300 total lines`.
defect: read_line_range reports one more line than wc -l for a newline-terminated file (issue: "Showing lines 1-200 of 2238 total lines" for a 2237-line file), here `of 301 total lines`.

fault location.explanation: originalLineCount = content.split('\n').length counts the empty element after the final newline as an extra line; PR #1806 adds countLines(), which drops a trailing empty element, and uses it here.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/vybestack/llxprt-code/pull/1806. read_line_range (and read_file with a range) call processSingleFileContent, which in v0.9.3 splits the text on '\n' and uses lines.length as originalLineCount. For a file that ends with a newline, split produces a trailing empty string, so the total is N+1 while wc -l reports N, and read_line_range prints that inflated total in its 'Showing lines X-Y of T total lines' status. Commit 100dd93 (PR #1806, 'Fixes #1753') introduces countLines(), which subtracts the trailing empty element, and uses it in processSingleFileContent and in ast_read_file. The fix first ships in v0.10.0; the pinned v0.11.0 contains it, so the case is tested at v0.9.3, the latest release before the issue was opened (2026-03-27).
